task: Make the marketing landing page more responsive and add entrance/scroll animations

acceptanceCriteria.claim: On page load, the hero eyebrow badge, heading, subtitle, and CTA buttons fade and slide upward into view in a staggered sequence, ending fully visible and legible
acceptanceCriteria.navigationHint: open the landing page root and let the hero finish its entrance animation

acceptanceCriteria.claim: On a 375px-wide mobile viewport, the hero's two call-to-action buttons ('Get started' and 'See a receipt') stack vertically as full-width buttons with no horizontal overflow or clipped text
acceptanceCriteria.navigationHint: open the landing page root on a narrow mobile viewport

acceptanceCriteria.claim: Scrolling to the 'What's in a receipt' section reveals the six feature cards cascading into view one after another (staggered), rather than all appearing at once
acceptanceCriteria.navigationHint: click the 'What's in a receipt' nav link and watch the feature grid animate in

plan: Add a CSS-only staggered entrance animation to the hero (eyebrow/h1/subtitle/cta/meta/mock) using animation-delay per element, add a pulsing glow to the eyebrow status dot, and extend the existing IntersectionObserver-driven `.reveal` mechanism so multi-card sections (feature grid, steps, contrast cards) cascade child-by-child via nth-child transition-delay instead of fading in as one block. Separately, add a `max-width: 480px` breakpoint so the hero CTA buttons stack full-width on narrow phones instead of center-wrapping unevenly, and simplify the receipt-mockup claim rows (hide the small screenshot swatch) so they don't feel cramped at that width.
decisions: Implemented the stagger with CSS transition-delay on child selectors instead of a second JS timer/observer, so RevealOnScroll.tsx stays untouched and the effect degrades safely if JS is slow to hydrate

Used a dedicated max-width: 480px breakpoint rather than widening the existing 820px/860px breakpoints, so the tablet layout (which already works) is untouched and only the tightest phone widths change
Kept all new animation under the existing prefers-reduced-motion guard so users who disable motion still get the fully visible, static layout instantly
rejectedAlternatives: A JS-driven stagger (setTimeout per card) — rejected in favor of declarative CSS transition-delay, which is simpler and keeps working even before hydration finishes
Continuous parallax/tilt hover effects on the hero mockup — rejected as unnecessary motion for a marketing page and harder to reconcile with prefers-reduced-motion
A hamburger mobile nav menu — out of scope for this pass; the nav already collapses to a single CTA under 860px and wasn't the reported pain point

promptLog.text: Update the landing page to be a little more responsive and add some animations, and use it as an example receipt.

Adding a staggered CSS entrance animation to the hero, a cascading reveal for the feature/steps/contrast cards, and a sub-480px breakpoint that stacks the hero CTA buttons full-width on narrow phones — then running receipts qa/build against three falsifiable, screenshot-provable claims.
